text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The powerful minister of Abuja capital territory Lieutenant-General Jeremiah Useni says there will be no run-off local council election in the capital; electoral commission ruled earlier that the poll should be re-run in three council areas where there were no clear winners.
- New violence in Nigeria's Delta state where 19 people have been killed over land dispute between Ijaw and Urhobo tribes.

- Fresh row imminent over payments due to oil firms from the government for their joint venture operations after companies disobey directive to open escrow accounts for the money now said to be $1.2 billion in arrears.
- Oil industry sources blame fuel scarcity on breakdown of units of Port Harcourt and Warri oil refineries.
- United Nations human rights commission meeting in Geneva will appoint a special envoy to investigate human rights in Nigeria if a resolution being spearheaded by Western countries is adopted.
- Government to build 10 more toll plazas to collect taxes on the use of highways, says works minister Major-General Abdulkareem Adisa.
- Central bank mops up 14 billion naira from circulation through sale of treasury bills.
- List of approved taxes for the three tiers of government is published; states to impose development levy of 100 naira on all taxable adults.
- Fuel scarcity to ease from Wednesday, says task force set up to combat what has become a perenial problem.
- Peugeot Nigeria Limited plans to export cars to North Africa, chief executive Francis Guoyon tells African international trade fair in Kaduna, northern Nigeria.
